title: Halloween gets an extra hour in South Florida
igCaption:
Halloween weekend in South Florida has clocks, cocktails, and a few costume stops. Oct. 31, prices vary

Sources: Local 10, Miami New Times

#SouthFlorida #Halloween #FortLauderdale #MiamiBeach

scenes.text: The Senate is unlikely to act this year on making daylight saving time permanent, so the clock change is still on.

Room 901 in Fort Lauderdale runs its Carrie takeover through Halloween. The hidden speakeasy inside Hyatt Centric Las Olas, at 100 E. Las Olas Blvd., has a 1970s prom setup, red-and-black decor, candlelight, dramatic florals, and Prom Punch.

scenes.text: Bar1939 at the National Hotel Miami Beach has three Halloween cocktails throughout October. The bar is inside the adults-only Art Deco hotel at 1677 Collins Ave., serving Morticia’s Bleeding Heart Margarita, Wednesday’s Woe, and Lurch’s Smoky Gin & Tonic. If you’re sipping Morticia’s here, check NEAR later and see who was there.

scenes.text: Halloween night has plenty going on in South Florida. And if Halloween had you crossing paths with someone all night without catching their name, NEAR is the part that lets you see who they were. Room 901 has the prom, Bar1939 has the cocktails, and the clock change is still in play.
